extra.message: SQL Injection via id parameter — Full read access to the users table (usernames/passwords) and blind/UNION-based extraction of arbitrary DB contents [verified: Line 30 concatenates params["id"] directly into SQL with no parameterization or sanitization.]

Insecure Deserialization leading to RCE via object parameter — Arbitrary code execution on the server via crafted pickle payload (e.g. os.system via __reduce__) [verified: Line 35 passes params["object"] directly to pickle.loads with zero validation.]

OS Command Injection via domain parameter — Arbitrary OS command execution as the server process user [verified: Line 39 concatenates params["domain"] into a shell=True subprocess command with no sanitization.]

Remote/Local File Inclusion leading to Code Execution via include parameter — Full arbitrary Python code execution by hosting a malicious file at an attacker-controlled or local path and referencing it via ?include= [verified: Line 56-57 fetches params["include"] (local path or URL) and execs the raw bytes with no restriction.]

SQL Injection / Authentication Bypass via password parameter — Authentication bypass allowing login as any user without valid credentials [verified: Line 67 sanitizes username via regex but password is concatenated raw into SQL WHERE clause, enabling classic auth bypass.]

Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Read / SSRF via path parameter — Read arbitrary files on the filesystem (e.g. /etc/passwd, source code) or make server-side requests to internal services (SSRF) [verified: Line 37 passes params["path"] to open()/urlopen() with only a scheme check, no traversal or SSRF restriction.]

XML External Entity (XXE) Injection via xml parameter — Local file disclosure and SSRF via crafted DOCTYPE/ENTITY definitions [verified: Line 41 parses params["xml"] with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False — full XXE.]

SQL Injection via comment parameter — Attacker can inject arbitrary SQL to manipulate or read database state via the comments table [verified: Line 50 uses %-formatting of params["comment"] directly into an INSERT statement, no escaping.]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via v parameter — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in victim's browser in the context of the vulnerable site [verified: Line 33 substitutes params["v"] into HTML via regex with no escaping.]

XPath Injection via name parameter — Bypass intended query logic and extract arbitrary XML node data (e.g. passwords) via crafted XPath predicates [verified: Line 43 string-formats params["name"] directly into an XPath expression with no escaping.]

Denial of Service via unbounded size parameter — Server memory exhaustion / hang from a single request with a large size value (e.g. size=9999999) [verified: Line 46 casts params["size"] to int and builds a string of that size squared with no upper bound, enabling memory/CPU exhaustion.]

Cross-Site Request Forgery on comment submission — An attacker can force an authenticated or unauthenticated victim's browser to submit arbitrary stored comments (or chain with the stored XSS at this same sink) simply by getting them to load an image/link, with no user interaction beyond a page visit [verified: Line 50's comment INSERT is triggered by a plain GET with no CSRF token/origin check/SameSite cookie, and DSVW's own CASES table documents this exact GET-based CSRF technique.]

Stored Cross-Site Scripting via comment display — Persistent JavaScript execution against any user who views the comments page [verified: Line 54 renders stored comment.text back via %-formatting into <td> with no escaping, and the comment itself is unsanitized at insertion (line 50).]

Open Redirect via redir parameter — Redirect victims to attacker-controlled phishing sites while appearing to originate from the trusted domain [verified: Line 61 inserts params["redir"] into a meta-refresh URL with no allow-list or validation.]

JSONP Callback Injection (XSS) via callback parameter — Arbitrary JavaScript execution by supplying a malicious callback value that breaks out of the intended function-call context [verified: Line 65 concatenates params["callback"] directly around JSON with no validation of characters.]

Predictable Session Token via insecure PRNG — Session ID prediction could allow session hijacking of authenticated users [verified: Line 68 uses random.sample (non-CSPRNG) to generate the 20-char SESSIONID.]

Verbose Error Messages / Stack Trace Disclosure — Leaks server file paths, internals, and code structure aiding further exploitation (also enables the 'Full Path Disclosure' / 'Source Code Disclosure' cases) [verified: Line 72 returns full traceback.format_exc() in the response body on any exception.]

HTTP Response Header Injection via charset parameter — Inject arbitrary headers or split the response to smuggle additional content/headers to the client (response splitting) [verified: Line 78 inserts params["charset"] into the Content-Type header with no CR/LF sanitization; though BaseHTTPRequestHandler's send_header may strip some, the raw value is unsanitized in application code.]
